lessons.title: What do you eat and drink?
lessons.tip:
Use "kan godt lide" for liking something and "vil gerne" for politely wanting something.
Example: Jeg kan godt lide kaffe, og jeg vil gerne have en kop.

What do you drink with the meal?

lessons.title: Do you like it?
lessons.tip:
To answer "Kan du lide …?" say "Ja, det kan jeg godt." or "Nej, det kan jeg ikke."
To agree: "Det kan jeg også." (positive) or "Det kan jeg heller ikke." (negative).

en: I do not like it either.

repeatLines.tip: "kan du lide" is pronounced roughly "ka du li"

lessons.title: How does it taste?
lessons.tip:
Describe taste with "Det smager" + adjective: Det smager godt / dårligt / fantastisk.
"Det er for" + adjective means "it is too …": Det er for salt.

sentences.en: It does not taste so good.

repeatLines.tip: "Det er for" is pronounced roughly "dee fɔ"

lessons.title: Eating then and now
lessons.tip:
To compare amounts use mere / mindre + noun + end.
Example: Jeg spiser mere frugt nu end før. (more fruit now than before)

lessons.title: Shops
lessons.tip:
Use "hos" for shops named after the person (hos bageren, hos slagteren), "i" for kiosk, supermarked and blomsterforretning, and "på" for apoteket.
Example: Jeg køber brød hos bageren.

lessons.title: Some: nogle and noget
lessons.tip:
Use "nogle" with countable things in the plural and "noget" with uncountable amounts.
Example: nogle æbler (some apples), noget vand (some water).

lessons.title: Containers
lessons.tip: A container or measure comes before the thing in it, with no word for "of": en pose æbler (a bag of apples), en flaske vin (a bottle of wine).

lessons.title: Money
lessons.tip: Say "kroner" only for whole amounts: ni kroner. With decimals say the two numbers: 2,95 = to femoghalvfems. 1,50 is "halvanden krone".

sentences.en: It costs one and a half kroner.

lessons.title: Asking about prices
lessons.tip:
Answer a price question with "den" for en-words, "det" for et-words and "de" for plurals.
Example: Hvad koster et æble? Det koster tre kroner.

lessons.title: Asking for things and amounts
lessons.tip:
Ask for things with "Jeg skal have …" or "Jeg vil gerne have …".
"noget" (uncountable) goes with "hvor meget"; "nogle" (countable) goes with "hvor mange".
